title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

reading.body:
This incident illustrates a deliberate attempt to manipulate AI-generated outputs by injecting fabricated source material into the information environment those systems draw on. A fictitious think tank was created to produce content that mimicked legitimate academic research, complete with citations from real organizations, in order to make the material appear credible to both human readers and AI retrieval and training pipelines. The method exploited a structural feature of large language models: they cannot independently verify the institutional legitimacy of sources they ingest, so content that looks authoritative can influence how those systems represent contested facts.

The failure mode is not one internal to any AI system's reasoning. It is an upstream poisoning attack, targeting the data layer before any model evaluation occurs. Catching it would have required either provenance verification at the point of ingestion, active monitoring for coordinated inauthentic content creation, or some mechanism for flagging newly created sources that publish at anomalous volume in a short window. None of those safeguards, if they existed, prevented the content from being published and potentially indexed.

What is not established is whether any AI system actually incorporated this material into its outputs, updated its training data on the basis of it, or changed the answers it gave users. The reporting describes an attempt and an intent, not a confirmed effect on any deployed model.

reports.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda

summary:
# Summary

Israeli officials and contractors set up a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute to spread pro-Israel propaganda through artificial intelligence systems. Between August 6 and 14, the site published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words designed to influence chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude. The reports presented Israel's position on contentious issues including alleged war crimes and genocide claims, framed as neutral academic research with citations from legitimate organizations. The operation was part of a broader campaign financed by tens of millions of dollars from the Israeli government and routed through intermediaries including European advertising company Havas Media.

The campaign represents an attempt to manipulate how AI systems present information about Israel by seeding content into training data repositories. Israeli officials have expressed frustration that these expensive public diplomacy efforts have failed to improve Israel's standing in American public opinion, which has shifted significantly toward Palestinians. Recent polling shows only 36 percent of Americans now sympathize with Israel compared to higher levels previously, with particularly steep declines among younger Americans. Experts warn this scheme demonstrates a new threat where foreign governments and others attempt to poison AI training data in ways users cannot easily verify.
